SAMPLE SIZE.evidence_source: Self-Liking: r(80) = 0.86, po.001; Self-Competence: r(80) = 0.66, po.001. The difference in correlation strength was significant, t(79) = 3.67, po0.001 (Steiger, 1980). Disattenuated correlations showed the same pattern, indicating that this finding is not a product of differential scale reliabilities, Self-Liking: r(80) = 0.96; Self-Competence: r(80) = 0.77. A simultaneous linear regression was performed with Self-Competence and Self-Liking entered as predictors of the RSES. Both predictors contributed unique variance, but Self-Liking was a much greater predictor (R2 = .79), Self-Liking: b = .71, t(79) = 11.54, po.001; Self-Competence: b = .28, t(79) = 4.52, po.001. Although the correlation between predictors was fairly strong in this regression, r(80) = .54, po.001, it did not reach the threshold at which multicollinearity typically becomes a problem (r4.90; Tabachnik & Fidell, 2001).

section_summary.extract_value: This 'Results' section details scale reliabilities for SDE, RSES, Self-Liking, Self-Competence, and Big Five personality traits. It then examines the relationships between RSES, Self-Liking, and Self-Competence, reporting correlations and regression analyses. Further, it investigates the associations between Self-Deception (SDE) and the self-evaluation measures, concluding with an analysis of personality trait profiles for these measures, noting differences in correlations with Conscientiousness and Openness.
